source: HYG Star Database v4.1 (astronexus/HYG-Database, hyg/CURRENT/hygdata_v41.csv) - David Nash; compiled from Hipparcos, Yale Bright Star and Gliese catalogs; distances in parsecs from parallaxes. License CC BY-SA 4.0 (this file's `stars` and distances are derived from it and so carry share-alike).
d3-celestial (github.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial) constellations.lines.json - Olaf Frohn; BSD-3-Clause. Stick-figure vertices (J2000 ra/dec) were matched to HYG stars by position (<0.12 deg).

Wikipedia 'IAU designated constellations' (names, abbreviations, genitives, meanings, origin, brightest star) and 'IAU designated constellations by solid angle' (area, rank, centre RA/Dec, quadrant) - CC BY-SA 4.0; underlying boundaries by E. Delporte for the IAU (1930). Families from Wikipedia 'Constellation family' (D. Menzel, A Field Guide to the Stars and Planets, 1975).
visible_months is computed here (constellation culminating around 21h local time), only for dec > -55 deg; story is a factual origin line assembled from the Wikipedia table, not folklore.
